# Standard library dependencies

<!-- Generated by `python -m tools.qualification.dependencies report --write`. Edit
     tools/qualification/stdlib-dependencies.toml, not this file. -->

The rule: a stdlib module requires first-party code and what its target's operating
system supplies. wgpu-native is the only general third-party exception. Feature-specific
runtime loads are restricted to their recorded source and target. `python -m
tools.qualification.dependencies check` enforces it on every manifest link record,
every system header a native source or module includes, every literal run-time load
and process launch, and every file that carries someone else's copyright notice. A
failure names the module, the target and the dependency.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FreeType | `GUI/FreeType/FreeTypeFace` | linux, macos, windows | headers `ft2build.h`; pkg-config `freetype2` | A first-party TrueType reader and rasterizer in BTRC behind the same face contract. |
| GTK 4 | `GUI/Shim/Shim` | linux | headers `cairo-ft.h`; headers `gdk/gdkkeysyms.h`; headers `gdk/wayland/gdkwayland.h`; headers `gdk/x11/gdkx.h`; headers `gtk/gtk.h`; headers `pango/pangocairo.h`; pkg-config `gtk4-wayland`; pkg-config `gtk4-x11`; pkg-config `gtk4` | First-party windows and controls over the display server's protocol. |
| alsa-lib | `Audio/Linux/LinuxAudioDevice` | linux | loads `libasound.so.2` | Kernel PCM, PulseAudio, PipeWire, and self-contained null/raw-file PCM routes use first-party code. Other configured ALSA plugins, including JACK-only routes, still need their installed libasound runtime. Retiring that compatibility path requires an owner decision. |
| curl | `HTTP/HTTPCurlTransport` | android, linux, macos | programs `curl` | Android, Linux and macOS use first-party code for plain HTTP and HTTP forward proxies. Linux also supports SOCKS4/4a/5/5h for plain HTTP. An installed curl handles explicit Proxy-Authorization fields on Linux SOCKS routes and optional SOCKS5 GSSAPI. iOS uses NSURLSession. macOS uses NSURLSession for direct HTTPS and ordinary HTTP CONNECT proxies, with installed curl preserving its configured trust store and unsupported proxy or request options. Android and Linux retain curl for HTTPS and remaining proxy paths. Windows uses WinHTTP. |
| dbus-launch (legacy X11 session activation) | `DBus/Linux/DBusTransportProvider` | linux | programs `dbus-launch` | Only a legacy X11 session without a reachable XDG bus socket or saved bus address needs the installed dbus-x11 service helper. Moving activation out of the stdlib or retiring automatic startup needs an owner decision. |
| libX11 | `GUI/Shim/Shim` | linux | headers `X11/Xlib.h`; pkg-config `x11` | Use native Wayland, including GPU presentation. Preserve inexpensive X11 compatibility without a new X11 backend. |
| libwayland-client | `GUI/Shim/Shim` | linux | headers `wayland-client.h`; pkg-config `wayland-client` | The Wayland wire protocol from first-party code, except where wgpu-native's surface needs the library's own objects. |
| musl's regex (bundled source) | `Regex` | windows | bundled `src/runtime/windows/musl` | A first-party matcher; Windows supplies no POSIX regex. |
| the WebView2 SDK (header and loader DLL) | `GUI/Shim/ShimWeb` | windows | loads `WebView2Loader.dll` | The COM declarations are first-party. The supported Win32 activation API is supplied by Microsoft's SDK loader. Decide whether to retain the loader or rely on the runtime's changeable internal export. |

## Standards data used by first-party implementations

- Unicode Character Database 17.0.0. The line-break and grapheme tables contain character properties. First-party code implements both algorithms. The audit checks the tables and their license by SHA-256. [Upstream data](https://github.com/unicode-org/unicodetools/tree/725fb6055cd42915c74bcf77b91aa8fb8ef18669/unicodetools/data/ucd/17.0.0)
  - `src/stdlib/GUI/Text/GraphemeData.h`
  - `src/stdlib/GUI/Text/LineBreakData.h`
  - `src/stdlib/GUI/Text/UNICODE-LICENSE.txt`

## Owner decisions

### A web view on Linux (WebKitGTK)

Move the Linux embedded web view into an optional WebKitGTK-backed package. Preserve
embedded rendering and provide a migration for existing IWebView clients. Keep the
existing implementation and its pending requirements until the package works.

### A Java VM on desktop systems (HotSpot)

Keep Library.Java on Android using the application's ART runtime. Move desktop VM
hosting, including createHost, into an optional JDK-backed package with a migration for
existing callers. Keep desktop checked-JNI tests under -Xcheck:jni.

### The display client library a Linux GPU surface needs

Target native Wayland. Ordinary windows and controls use a first-party client of the
compositor protocol. GPU presentation may use libwayland-client as part of the
wgpu-native surface integration. The driver requires a real wl_display and wl_surface
owned by the same connection. Limit the allowance to GPU windows and verify actual loads.
Preserve X11 compatibility where inexpensive. Do not undertake a new X11 backend or
require Xwayland for a Wayland session.

### TLS on Linux

Build first-party TLS over the first-party cryptography and the system CA bundle.
Qualify certificate and hostname verification, protocol interoperability and observable
HTTP behavior. Obtain independent security review before switching production HTTPS.
Keep the current working transport while qualification and review are pending.

## What each operating system supplies, as the stdlib uses it

- **android**: classes: `android.app.*`, `android.content.*`, `android.graphics.*`, `android.hardware.*`, `android.net.*`, `android.os.*`, `android.text.*`, `android.util.*`, `android.view.*`, `android.webkit.*`, `android.widget.*`, `java.io.*`, `java.nio.*`, `java.util.*`; libraries: `android`, `log`
- **ios**: frameworks: `CoreFoundation`, `CoreGraphics`, `CoreImage`, `CoreText`, `Foundation`, `IOSurface`, `ImageIO`, `Metal`, `QuartzCore`, `Security`, `UIKit`, `WebKit`
- **linux**: libraries: `util`; programs: `/bin/sh`
- **macos**: frameworks: `AVFoundation`, `AppKit`, `AudioToolbox`, `CFNetwork`, `CoreAudio`, `CoreFoundation`, `CoreGraphics`, `CoreMedia`, `CoreText`, `CoreVideo`, `Foundation`, `IOSurface`, `ImageIO`, `QuartzCore`, `Security`, `WebKit`; libraries: `bsm`; programs: `/bin/sh`
- **windows**: libraries: `bcrypt`, `comctl32`, `dwmapi`, `gdi32`, `ole32`, `oleaut32`, `shell32`, `shlwapi`, `user32`, `uuid`, `winhttp`, `ws2_32`
